source: NCERT Class VII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Geography Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. India's Monsoon Climate
points: India has a **tropical monsoon** type of climate, dominated by the **seasonal reversal of winds (the monsoon)**.
The word **monsoon** comes from the Arabic **'mausim'** = season.
The year has broadly **four seasons**: **winter, summer, the rainy (south-west monsoon), and the retreating monsoon (autumn)**.

sections.heading: 2. The Four Seasons
points: **Winter (Dec–Feb):** cold, dry; northern plains coldest; some rain in the NW from **western disturbances** and in the SE (Tamil Nadu) from the **retreating/NE monsoon**.
**Summer (Mar–May):** hot; hot dry winds (**loo**) in the north; low pressure builds up.
**South-West Monsoon (Jun–Sep):** the main **rainy season** — moisture-laden winds from the **Arabian Sea** and **Bay of Bengal** bring most of India's rainfall.
**Retreating Monsoon (Oct–Nov):** the monsoon withdraws; humid, giving rain to the **south-east coast**.

sections.heading: 3. Factors Affecting India's Climate
points: **Latitude** — the **Tropic of Cancer** passes through the middle of India; the south is hotter.
**Altitude** — hills/mountains are cooler; the **Himalayas** block cold Central Asian winds.
**Distance from the sea** — coastal areas have a **moderate (maritime)** climate; interiors have **extreme (continental)** climate.
**Relief/mountains** — the **Western Ghats** force winds up, giving heavy rain on the windward side and a **rain shadow** on the leeward side.

sections.heading: 4. Regional Variation
points: Rainfall is very **uneven**: **Mawsynram/Cherrapunji** (Meghalaya) are among the **wettest** places on Earth; **Rajasthan (Thar)** is very **dry**.
Temperature varies from freezing in the Himalayas to very hot in the deserts.
The **monsoon** is the key to Indian **agriculture** — its timing and amount decide the harvest.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: India = tropical monsoon climate; monsoon from Arabic 'mausim' (season).
Seasons: winter, summer, SW monsoon (main rains, Jun–Sep), retreating monsoon (Oct–Nov).
SW monsoon from Arabian Sea & Bay of Bengal; retreating monsoon → SE coast (Tamil Nadu) rain.
Climate factors: latitude (Tropic of Cancer), altitude, distance from sea, relief (rain shadow).
Wettest: Mawsynram/Cherrapunji (Meghalaya); driest: Thar (Rajasthan).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **south-west monsoon (Jun–Sep)** brings **most** of India's rain.
**Tamil Nadu** gets much of its rain from the **retreating/north-east monsoon (Oct–Nov)**, not the SW monsoon.
The **leeward (rain-shadow) side** of the Western Ghats is **dry**; the windward (west) side is wet.
The **Tropic of Cancer** divides India into roughly tropical (south) and subtropical (north).
